findings.title: C15 permits partial retirement when the trial receipt is not clean
findings.body: C15 gates each of the six pieces independently on its own `not needed` receipt line. The authority instead makes the six an all-or-nothing set: if the background-session receipt is not clean, all six remain plain keeps. A mixed receipt could therefore delete five pieces even though one remaining need makes the receipt non-clean.
findings.suggestion: Add a global clean-receipt prerequisite to the What and DoD: if any of the six is still needed, keep all six with their markers. Only after the receipt is clean may the six retire. Replace the tautological final clause in DoD line 6 with an explicit failing condition for deletion without that global prerequisite.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B6 says, “if the receipt does not come back clean, the six pieces stay as plain keeps”; register R15 repeats “otherwise all six stay.” C15 instead says each piece leaves when its individual line says it is not needed.

findings.title: The hand-landed counter-specimen is expected to refuse too strongly
findings.body: The DoD requires all must-refuse counter-specimens to refuse outright. Under the stamped provenance option, the well-formed hand-landed-envelope specimen is only prohibited from receiving `full-panel-confirmed`; it may be accepted as `audited-chain`. The current criterion can force implementation back toward rejecting legitimate hand-landed work.
findings.suggestion: State separate expected outcomes for the three counter-specimens. In particular, require the well-formed hand-landed envelope to refuse `full-panel-confirmed` while preserving the stamped `audited-chain` behavior, and re-cut the fixture expectation accordingly.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D2 says that under option (a) the second counter-specimen “refuses full-panel certification rather than all certification” and that the fixture pair is re-cut to the stamped resolution. C12 says without qualification that “the must-refuse counter-specimens refuse.”

findings.title: No negative case proves that missing class closure refuses certification
findings.body: The receipt writer is required to read both the revisit trigger and the class-closure line on an out-of-scope follow-up. The DoD tests only a missing revisit trigger. C13's successful fixture includes class closure, so it would still pass if the writer silently ignored that field.
findings.suggestion: Add a fixture or dry run whose otherwise-valid follow-up omits class closure and require the writer to refuse it, naming the missing artifact. Include the applicable `none` assertion case so non-class findings remain representable.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D8 states that revisit trigger and class closure are both required lines “read by the writer and the vet.” Register R6 likewise requires both. C12's sole negative follow-up criterion covers only the missing trigger.

findings.title: C12's new D1 rows have no owner for their required closing work
findings.body: The map allocates all of FR-D8's table-change criterion to C13, although that criterion explicitly requires the receipt writer and four checks built by C12 to be added as new D1 rows. C12 quotes R26 but has no DoD for adding, re-verifying, or closing those rows; C13 only closes rows it touches. Thus the writer/check rows can escape the mandated final annex correction.
findings.suggestion: Split FR-D8 bullet 11 between C12 and C13. Add a C12 DoD requiring the writer and four-check rows, build-head re-verification, live-declaration move, and dated closing note; retain C13 ownership of the loop-state rows.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-D8 says “The receipt writer and the four checks are new rows the certification child adds” and requires a dated annex note. Register R26 assigns closing work separately to C10, C11, C12, and C13, while the coverage map assigns this acceptance bullet solely to C13.

findings.title: C11 does not carry the required result-shape transition note
findings.body: C11 moves engine result channels and shapes but neither its What nor its DoD updates the release transition note. C10's transition criterion covers only dropped, renamed, or newly required arguments, so no child grades disclosure of the result-shape changes.
findings.suggestion: Add a C11 DoD requiring the same release's transition note to enumerate every result-channel and result-shape change made by C11, coordinated with C10's argument-transition section.
findings.evidence: Spec B FR-S1 requires the transition note to cover “the result shape as well as the entry surface.” Register R24 expressly lists C11 as a transition-note consumer. C11's DoD contains no transition-note criterion.

findings.title: C12 lands new checks before the keep-or-retire list can satisfy their birth duty
findings.body: C12 creates the receipt writer and four new checks in Wave 1, while C6 creates the keep-or-retire reference and its entries only in Wave 2. The new checks therefore exist for at least one landing without the retirement-condition entries required at birth, and C12 has no seam to create those entries itself.
findings.suggestion: Make the keep-or-retire document available before C12 lands, or sequence C12 after C6 and require C12 to add entries for the writer/check components in its own PR. Update R16's consumers and C12's DoD so the entries, conditions, tags, and readers are graded at birth.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B2 says the three duties bind “at birth: new detectors from the stamp forward.” Spec B FR-D8 identifies the receipt writer and four checks as new and explicitly assigns them a birth bite-proof. The package sequences C12 in Wave 1 and C6 in Wave 2.

findings.title: C6 drops the consumer-report lifecycle allocated to it
findings.body: C6 grades creation of the label and template but omits the acceptance criterion's operational half: link each report from the component entry, close it after a pass reads it or its proposal is ruled, treat silence as unmeasured, and contact known consumers before retirement while waiting at most one gardening window. A builder can satisfy C6 while leaving consumer evidence disconnected or treating silence as consent.
findings.suggestion: Carry the full consumer-report lifecycle into C6's What and add a DoD criterion exercising report linkage, closure, unmeasured handling, and the bounded pre-retirement consumer inquiry.
findings.evidence: Spec A FR-B3 lines 669–676 mandate linkage, closure, silence-as-unmeasured, and the one-window inquiry. Coverage-map row 74 assigns that entire acceptance bullet to C6, whose DoD checks only that the label and four template fields exist.

findings.title: Skill descriptions are promised but absent from C7's DoD
findings.body: C7's What promises to rewrite skill descriptions as always-loaded pointers, but every DoD criterion is limited to charters, reference pages, measurements, and stack behavior. The PR can pass without changing or validating the descriptions.
findings.suggestion: Add a DoD bullet enumerating the affected skill descriptions and verifying that each is a pointer that says when to load its referenced mechanism.
